headline: KPMG Flags 1.25M Healthcare AI Skill Gap in India Report
summary: KPMG and FICCI published a joint report this week stating India needs to skill 1.25 million healthcare professionals annually in AI and digital health. Read as a strategic signal: KPMG is building offshore healthcare AI delivery capacity at scale. This compresses margins on implementation work and signals that Big Four firms are positioning to deliver clinical AI engagements at lower cost structures globally. Booz Allen's separate Anthropic partnership for critical infrastructure AI this week reinforces the pattern: major consulting and government services firms are embedding specific AI models into their delivery methodology.
so_what: KPMG's FICCI report says India needs to skill 1.25 million healthcare workers annually in AI and digital health. This is not an India story. It's a signal that KPMG is building offshore healthcare AI delivery capacity at scale, which changes the cost structure of AI implementation services globally.
original_title: Skilling India's healthcare workforce for digital health and AI
